title.narrative: Climate smart livestock value chain development for Sierra Leone

description.narrative: Overall Objective: Improving food and nutrition security and strengthening resilience and adaptation to the impacts of climate change in the Moyamba and Karene districts of Sierra Leone.

Overall objective: Improving food and nutrition security and strengthening resilience and adaptation to the impacts of climate change in the Moyamba and Karene districts of Sierra Leone.Project objectives: 1. strengthened systems of production, processing and marketing;2. utilization of solar energy in the production and preservation processes of organic food crops and promoting of LANN;3. Introduction of improved dual purpose resilient indigenous poultry breeds, rabbit and grass cutter value chain development; and4. Pilot integrated poultry-fish farming.

The direct target group of the project are 2,000 vulnerable smallholder households, i.e. 1,000 households each in Karene and Moyamba districts. With a national average household size of 5.9 persons, a total of 11,800 persons will directly benefit from the project. At least 50% of the targeted project participants are women. Project participants will be selected by the project team in consultation with relevant ministries (agriculture and marine resources) and community stakeholders (traditional leaders) who will jointly develop a selection criterion. The following criteria will be considered: needy members (wealth ranking), age (youth), gender, current farming activities, farming experience, residence in the target community, interest in becoming an active member of an FBO or VSLA, interest in a particular value chain. There is no overlap of the target group with previous or ongoing projects.Indirect target groups at the institutional level include the staff of relevant ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs), including the MAFS with 12 staff (6 per district) and 7 heads of department and 2 staff of NGO departments of the ministry, making a total of 21 people, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) (6 staff), SLARI (2 staff members), MFMR (2 staff members), PMB (2 staff members), Ministry of Youth Affairs (MoYA, 2 staff members), Ministry of Gender (MoG, 2 staff members), Chiefdom and District Councils (6 members and 6 staff members of the District Councils), i.e. a total of 49 (indirect project participants) who participate in project activities in their respective functions (i.e., monitoring missions). These governmental and non-governmental actors will also act as multipliers for the project and promote sustainability by monitoring activities after the project cycle, as it is the mandate of the government to address food and nutrition issues in the communities.
